scope: Two known, curated product branches from geranyl diphosphate; no enzyme-activity, odor, isotope-enrichment or yield prediction.

numbering.definition: Persistent carbon lineage labels, not a universal product atom-numbering system. GPP C1 is the carbon attached to the diphosphate oxygen; C1–C8 follow the eight-carbon main chain, C9 is the methyl at C3, and C10 is the second methyl at C7.
numbering.symmetry_note: The unlabeled connectivity graph admits a swap of the two methyl carbons attached to GPP C7. C8/C10 select one representative map; a position-specific isotope experiment would require its own stereochemical and mechanistic specification. This graph ambiguity does not assert that the two methyl groups have identical spectroscopic environments.
numbering.tracer_scope: A selected carbon label illustrates this declared map only. It does not predict enrichment, exchange, mixtures, fluxes or kinetic isotope effects.

protonation_note: Full equations below use the neutral species represented in the PubChem snapshots so formula and formal-charge balance can be checked explicitly. Enzyme databases often use charged species and different proton conventions; the neutral equations are not physiological proton stoichiometry claims. Carbon-only diagrams omit water and diphosphate for readability.

gpp.name: (2E)-Geranyl diphosphate
gpp.representation: Neutral diphosphoric-acid ester as returned by PubChem; not a claim about its predominant physiological protonation state.

limonene.name: (4R)-(+)-Limonene
limonene.representation: The R enantiomer documented for the selected Citrus sinensis enzyme. Source compound numbering calls this center C4; its lineage label here is C6.

linalool.name: (3R)-(−)-Linalool
linalool.representation: The R enantiomer documented for the selected Lavandula angustifolia enzyme.

reactions.title: Fold the carbon chain into a ring

steps.title: Activate the allylic diphosphate
steps.text: The enzyme promotes diphosphate departure in a metal-supported active site. The resulting allylic chemistry occurs in the enzyme, not as an unconstrained carbocation in solution.

steps.title: Reorient and close the ring
steps.text: The canonical mechanistic model includes allylic isomerization through linalyl diphosphate, allowing reorientation before cyclization. In the displayed carbon map, ring closure joins C1 and C6.

steps.title: Release a hydrocarbon
steps.text: Proton loss terminates the cyclization sequence to give limonene. All ten substrate carbons remain, and the enzyme-selected product is the (4R) enantiomer.

reactions.mechanism_status: Curated explanatory mechanism; the graph changes validate net carbon connectivity, not the existence or lifetime of every intermediate.

reactions.title: Capture water without closing a ring

steps.title: Activate the same precursor
steps.text: The linalool branch starts from geranyl diphosphate, the same ten-carbon precursor as the limonene branch.

steps.title: Capture water at the allylic center
steps.text: Water capture yields an acyclic tertiary alcohol. In this representative carbon map, the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is C3 and the C2–C3 double bond becomes C1–C2. The carbon skeleton does not form a ring.

steps.title: Retain the enzyme-selected stereochemistry
steps.text: The selected lavender enzyme produces (3R)-linalool. This route is not an oxidation of limonene; the net reaction consumes water and releases diphosphate.

reactions.mechanism_status: Curated explanatory account consistent with the net catalytic annotation; detailed water/proton trajectories are not inferred from the carbon map.
